accepted.s: Anandibai Joshi is associated with which of the following achievements?
o: First woman D.Sc. from an Indian university
First woman admitted to the Indian Institute of Science
First Indian woman to earn a degree in Western medicine
First Indian woman to obtain a Ph.D. in science
accepted.x: Anandibai Joshi became the first Indian woman to earn a degree in Western medicine, obtaining an M.D. from the Woman's Medical College of Pennsylvania in 1886.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the person associated with a distinctive first achievement.
accepted.sec: Women scientists - FIRST achievements and field

accepted.s:
With reference to Janaki Ammal, consider the following statements:
1. She pioneered plant breeding and worked on sugarcane hybrids at Coimbatore.
2. She co-authored the book Chromosome Atlas of Cultivated Plants.
3. She was awarded the Padma Shri in 1977.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Janaki Ammal was a botanist and cytogeneticist associated with plant breeding, sugarcane hybrids, the cited book and the Padma Shri of 1977.
accepted.tq: Combine several precise biographical facts and test whether all statements belong to the same scientist.
accepted.sec: Women scientists - FIRST achievements and field

accepted.s: Kamala Sohonie was the first woman to be admitted to which institution?
o: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science
accepted.x: Kamala Sohonie was the first woman admitted to the Indian Institute of Science. She was a biochemist who later obtained her Ph.D. from Cambridge.
accepted.tq: Use an institutional first to distinguish a scientist from other prominent women scientists.
accepted.sec: Women scientists - FIRST achievements and field

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Asima Chatterjee — First woman General President of the Indian Science Congress
Anna Mani — First woman D.Sc. from an Indian university
Bibha Chowdhuri — Pioneer of sugarcane hybridisation
Janaki Ammal — First woman General President of the Indian Science Congress
accepted.x: Asima Chatterjee became the first woman General President of the Indian Science Congress in 1975. Janaki Ammal was associated with plant breeding, Anna Mani with meteorology, and Bibha Chowdhuri with particle physics.
accepted.tq: Use a wrong-person-with-a-deed trap to separate closely related biographical achievements.
accepted.sec: Women scientists - FIRST achievements and field

accepted.s:
Asima Chatterjee is associated with which of the following contributions?
1. Development of the anti-epileptic drug Ayush-56
2. Development of anti-malarial drugs
3. Becoming the first woman D.Sc. from an Indian university
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Asima Chatterjee was an organic chemist who obtained the first woman D.Sc. from an Indian university in 1944 and worked on Ayush-56 and anti-malarial drugs.
accepted.tq: Recognise a cluster of achievements belonging to one scientist rather than splitting them across different persons.
accepted.sec: Women scientists - FIRST achievements and field

accepted.s: Anna Mani is popularly known as the ‘Weather Woman of India’ primarily because of her work in which field?
o: Meteorological instruments, solar radiation and wind energy
Cosmic rays, mesons and particle detectors
accepted.x: Anna Mani contributed to making India self-reliant in meteorological instruments and worked on solar radiation and wind energy. She also served as Deputy Director-General of the India Meteorological Department.
accepted.tq: Infer the field from the descriptive title and the associated applications.
accepted.sec: Women scientists - FIRST achievements and field

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Bibha Chowdhuri is correct?
o: She pioneered plant breeding at Coimbatore.
She founded the Bose Institute at Kolkata.
She formulated the equation of thermal ionisation.
She worked on cosmic rays and mesons with D.M. Bose.
accepted.x: Bibha Chowdhuri worked on cosmic rays and mesons with D.M. Bose and completed her Ph.D. under P.M.S. Blackett. The star HD 86081 was named ‘Bibha’ by the IAU in 2019.
accepted.tq: Eliminate options by matching each scientist with the specialised field stated in the question.
accepted.sec: Women scientists - FIRST achievements and field

accepted.s: The Raman Effect was discovered by C.V. Raman on 28 February 1928 at which institution?
o: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science, Kolkata
accepted.x: C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science in Kolkata.
accepted.tq: Link the exact date of a discovery with its location and institution.
accepted.sec: C.V. Raman - discovery, Nobel year, institutions, day commemorating

accepted.s: C.V. Raman worked at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science outside office hours while serving in which office?
o: Indian Institute of Science administration, Calcutta
Office of the Director-General of Meteorology, Calcutta
Office of the Atomic Energy Commission, Calcutta
accepted.x: From 1907, C.V. Raman worked at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science outside office hours while employed in the Accountant General's Office, Calcutta. He did so at the invitation of Amrit Lal Sircar.
accepted.tq: Test the unusual combination of workplace, research institution and period of service.
accepted.sec: C.V. Raman - discovery, Nobel year, institutions, day commemorating

accepted.s: Who invited C.V. Raman to work at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science?
accepted.x: Amrit Lal Sircar invited C.V. Raman to work at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the person connected with a specific professional opportunity.
accepted.sec: C.V. Raman - discovery, Nobel year, institutions, day commemorating

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about C.V. Raman:
1. He founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934.
2. He founded the Raman Research Institute in Bengaluru in 1948.
3. He was the first Indian director of the Indian Institute of Science.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Raman founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934 and the Raman Research Institute in 1948, and became the first Indian director of the Indian Institute of Science.
accepted.tq: Check a chronological institutional career through multiple statements.
accepted.sec: C.V. Raman - discovery, Nobel year, institutions, day commemorating

accepted.s: Which of the following musical instruments did C.V. Raman study in relation to their harmonic nature?
accepted.x: C.V. Raman was the first to study the harmonic nature of the tabla and mridangam.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a less commonly remembered contribution from the scientist’s better-known optical work.
accepted.sec: C.V. Raman - discovery, Nobel year, institutions, day commemorating

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Indian scientific institutions in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Raman Research Institute
B. Establishment of the Indian Academy of Sciences
C. Establishment of the Bose Institute
D. Establishment of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research
accepted.x: The Bose Institute was founded in 1917, the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934, TIFR in 1945 and the Raman Research Institute in 1948.
accepted.tq: Arrange institutions by their foundation years, using the earliest and latest events first.
accepted.sec: C.V. Raman - discovery, Nobel year, institutions, day commemorating

accepted.s: Homi Bhabha is popularly known as the:
accepted.x: Homi Bhabha is known as the Father of India's nuclear programme.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Atomic Energy Commission — First chairman, Homi Bhabha, 1948
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre — Founded by Homi Bhabha in 1945
accepted.x: The Atomic Energy Establishment at Trombay was founded in 1954 and was renamed BARC after Homi Bhabha's death in 1966. It was not founded as BARC in 1945.
accepted.tq: Find the institution-year statement that reverses the original name and later renaming.
accepted.sec: Homi Bhabha - titles, institutions, programme, awards

accepted.s: Who was the first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission of India?
accepted.x: Homi Bhabha was the first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission in 1948.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct authority-holder in an institutional leadership question.
accepted.sec: Homi Bhabha - titles, institutions, programme, awards

accepted.s: Homi Bhabha’s three-stage nuclear power programme was conceived as a:
accepted.x: Homi Bhabha conceived India's three-stage nuclear power programme as a thorium-based programme.
accepted.tq: Connect a national programme with its underlying resource base.
accepted.sec: Homi Bhabha - titles, institutions, programme, awards

accepted.s:
Which of the following contributions is associated with Homi Bhabha?
1. Bhabha scattering involving electrons and positrons
2. Cascade theory of cosmic-ray showers
3. Development of the Saha ionisation equation
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Bhabha scattering and the cascade theory of cosmic-ray showers are associated with Homi Bhabha. The Saha ionisation equation was formulated by Meghnad Saha.
accepted.tq: Use a nearby-scientist substitution as the false statement in a specialised-work question.
accepted.sec: Homi Bhabha - titles, institutions, programme, awards

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Award or distinction)
a. Adams Prize
b. Fellowship of the Royal Society
c. Padma Bhushan

d. Presidency of the first UN Conference on Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy

List-II (Year)
i. 1941
ii. 1942
iii. 1954
iv. 1955
accepted.x: Homi Bhabha received the Adams Prize in 1942, became a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1941, received the Padma Bhushan in 1954 and presided over the 1955 Geneva conference.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure year-pair and match the remaining awards chronologically.

accepted.s: Homi Bhabha died in which incident and in which year?
o: A laboratory accident in Trombay in 1954
An air crash over the Alps in 1948
A mountaineering accident in Geneva in 1955
An air crash on Mont Blanc in 1966
accepted.x: Homi Bhabha died in an Air India crash on Mont Blanc in 1966.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive event-location-year combination rather than the scientist’s general field.

o: Response in the Living and Non-Living — J.C. Bose

The Nervous Mechanism of Plants — Homi Bhabha
accepted.x: Response in the Living and Non-Living is a work of J.C. Bose. Chromosome Atlas of Cultivated Plants is associated with Janaki Ammal, while the other pairings are incorrect.

accepted.x: Thermal ionisation of elements is associated with Meghnad Saha. Ramanujan worked on number theory, partitions, infinite series, continued fractions and mock theta functions.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: S.N. Bose — Quantum statistics and bosons
Birbal Sahni — Engineering and Diwan of Mysore
accepted.x: S.N. Bose is associated with quantum statistics and bosons. Prafulla Chandra Ray worked in chemistry, Birbal Sahni in palaeobotany, and Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar with CSIR.

accepted.s: M. Visvesvaraya served as the Diwan of Mysore during which period?
accepted.x: M. Visvesvaraya, associated with engineering, served as the Diwan of Mysore from 1912 to 1919.

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations is correctly matched?
o: C.V. Raman — Light scattering and acoustics
Ramanujan — Nuclear physics and cosmic rays
accepted.x: C.V. Raman worked on light scattering, optics and acoustics. J.C. Bose worked on plant physiology and radio or microwave physics, S.N. Bose on quantum statistics, and Ramanujan on number theory.
accepted.tq: Use area-based elimination to separate scientists whose names and fields are easily confused.

accepted.s: The Saha equation was formulated by Meghnad Saha from his theory of:
accepted.x: Meghnad Saha formulated the Saha, or ionisation, equation from his theory of thermal ionisation of elements.

Age and chemical composition of plants
Mass and rotation of planets only

Speed and direction of ocean currents

Growth rate and water content of plants

accepted.s: Which statement best describes Meghnad Saha’s contribution to river planning in India?
o: He prepared the original plan for the Damodar Valley Project.
He designed the first irrigation project on the Krishna River.
He founded the first river-water tribunal in India.
He established the Central Water Commission.
